paragraphs.text: This area has 10 documented events, and 5 of them have approximate locations.
The founding of Tenochtitlan, on an island in Lake Texcoco, is conventionally dated to 1325, though the exact date is unclear.
Moctezuma I, born here in 1398 (approximate location), later became the fifth king of Tenochtitlan.
The Mexico Flood of 1446 is placed here approximately.
Moctezuma II, born here in 1466 (approximate location), later became the ninth emperor of the Aztec Empire.
In 1473 Tenochtitlan fought the Battle of Tlatelolco against Tlatelolco, its neighbour on the island.
On 19 February 1475 an earthquake struck Tenochtitlan during the reign of Tlatoani Axayacatl.
Cuauhtémoc, born here in 1495 (approximate location), later became the last Aztec Emperor.
A smallpox epidemic in Tenochtitlan from 1519 to 1520 is placed approximately.
On 22 May 1520, during the Spanish conquest, the Feast of Toxcatl ended in a massacre of Mexica elites.
On 30 June 1521 the Mexica won the Battle of Colhuacatonco, regarded as their most important victory of the siege of Tenochtitlan.
Tenochtitlan fell in 1521 to the Spanish and thousands of indigenous allies, especially Tlaxcaltec warriors.
The cocoliztli epidemic of 1545 to 1548, placed approximately, brought high fevers and bleeding.
The Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral, dated to 1570, sits on the former Aztec sacred precinct.
The Francisco Hernández expedition of 1570 to 1577 and a cocoliztli epidemic of 1576 to 1577 are also placed approximately.
